title: Characteristic Equation and Its Roots
quickIdea: det(A - lambda I) = 0 is a polynomial equation of degree n; its n roots, counted with multiplicity and over the complex numbers, are exactly the eigenvalues.
remember: det(A - lambda I) and det(lambda I - A) differ only by the factor (-1)^n, so they have the same roots; either form is safe.
2x2 shortcut: lambda^2 - (tr A) lambda + det A = 0.
3x3: lambda^3 - s1 lambda^2 + s2 lambda - det A = 0, where s1 = tr A and s2 is the sum of the three principal 2x2 minors.
An n x n matrix has n eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, but it may have fewer than n distinct real eigenvalues, and over the reals it may have none at all.
The coefficient of lambda^(n-1) is -tr A and the constant term is (-1)^n det A, which is exactly where sum = trace and product = determinant come from.

example.prompt: Find the characteristic polynomial of A = [[1,2,3],[0,4,5],[0,0,6]] and read off its eigenvalues.
example.work: A is upper triangular, so det(A - lambda I) = (1-lambda)(4-lambda)(6-lambda). Expanding: tr A = 11, det A = 24, and the principal minors are 1x4 = 4, 1x6 = 6, 4x6 = 24, so s2 = 34. The polynomial is lambda^3 - 11 lambda^2 + 34 lambda - 24.
example.answer: Eigenvalues 1, 4, 6. Check: 1+4+6 = 11 = tr A and 1x4x6 = 24 = det A.

gateAngle: Almost no GATE question needs the full cubic. 2016 Set 1 Q.5 and 2024 Set 1 Q.2 are settled by the product of the eigenvalues alone, 2025 Set 1 Q.31 by the 2x2 quadratic, and a triangular matrix by its diagonal. Build the polynomial only when the matrix is small and has no visible structure.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A is 3x3 with tr A = 6, det A = 6, and one eigenvalue equal to 1. Find the other two.
variations.why: The other two satisfy lambda2 + lambda3 = 6 - 1 = 5 and lambda2 lambda3 = 6/1 = 6, so they are the roots of t^2 - 5t + 6, namely 2 and 3. No cubic needs to be written.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does every real 3x3 matrix have at least one real eigenvalue?
variations.answer: Its characteristic polynomial has degree 3 with real coefficients, and a real polynomial of odd degree takes both signs at infinity, so it has a real root by the intermediate value theorem.
variations.why: This is the reason a real matrix of odd order can never have all its eigenvalues non-real, which is the argument GATE CSE 2016 Set 1 Q.5 relies on.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A 4x4 real matrix has characteristic polynomial lambda^4 - 5 lambda^3 + 7 lambda^2 - 3 lambda. What follows at once?
variations.answer: 0 is an eigenvalue and A is singular, because the constant term is 0 and the constant term is det A.
variations.why: The constant term of the characteristic polynomial of an n x n matrix is (-1)^n det A, so a zero constant term means a zero determinant.

trap.what: Assuming an n x n real matrix has n real eigenvalues, or that a repeated root of the polynomial is somehow not a separate eigenvalue.
trap.why: The polynomial has degree n over the complex numbers, so it always has n roots there, but a real matrix can have non-real roots, and multiplicity counts.
trap.counterexample: A = [[0,-1],[1,0]] gives lambda^2 + 1 = 0, so the eigenvalues are i and -i: two eigenvalues, no real one. A = [[2,1],[0,2]] gives (2-lambda)^2 = 0, so 2 is an eigenvalue of multiplicity 2.

check.question: A is 2x2 with tr A = 7 and det A = 12. What are its eigenvalues?
check.explanation: lambda^2 - 7 lambda + 12 = (lambda-3)(lambda-4) = 0. Sum 7 and product 12 agree with the trace and determinant, which is the check that the answer is right.
